open_positions.thesis: AAPL dropped only 0.98% today versus SPY's 1.91% and QQQ's 2.67%, showing clear relative strength during a broad selloff. Healthcare and Financials leading sector rotation suggests capital is seeking quality defensives, and AAPL fits that profile. With Extreme Fear at 12 and RSI likely pulling back toward oversold, a bounce toward the $368 area is a high-probability mean reversion trade into week-end flows.
open_positions.source: Watchlist + Sector Rotation + Relative Strength Analysis

open_positions.thesis: Consumer Discretionary is today's leading sector at +1.79%, significantly outperforming all other sectors. With WMT earnings on 11/19 as a potential catalyst and holiday travel/spending season approaching (AAA forecasting continued travel demand despite cost concerns), the sector has tailwinds. Extreme Fear readings historically compress quickly in consumer-facing sectors when spending data holds up. Sector leadership often persists for 5-10 sessions during rotation regimes.

OKTG surged 24.1% today on 1.5x average volume with RSI at 49.4 — meaning this massive move hasn't even pushed it into overbought territory, suggesting significant room to run. Price is still well below the 50SMA at $50.91, giving a clear technical magnet target. Relative strength vs SPY of +24.41% today is exceptional and flags institutional interest. The combination of high volume breakout + sub-50 RSI + gap to 50SMA is a high-conviction continuation setup.

Energy is the strongest relative sector today, only down 0.65% vs SPY's 1.96% decline — outperforming SPY by 1.31%. In a rising rate environment with strong GDP, energy tends to hold up as an inflation beneficiary. XLE shows clear relative strength leadership that typically persists for several sessions during risk-off rotations.

UVIX is up 27.61% today and was our biggest winner at +36.62% in the paper portfolio. With VIX at 35.89 and the selloff driven by structural macro concerns (5% 10Y yield, Nvidia subpoena, tech de-risking), volatility has room to expand further. The extreme fear regime (F&G=12) with no near-term catalyst for stabilization supports continued VIX elevation. UVIX shows massive relative strength vs SPY at +31.25% today.

Healthcare (XLV) was the clear relative strength leader today, down only 0.12% while XLK lost 7.27% and SPY fell 3.64%. In sustained selloffs, capital rotates into defensive sectors, and healthcare's resilience today signals institutional accumulation. With extreme fear persisting and no tech recovery catalyst in sight, the sector rotation trade into XLV has strong momentum tailwinds for the next week.

SOXS (3x inverse semiconductors) surged 31.71% today as the Nvidia subpoena news hammered the entire chip complex. RSI at 67.9 is elevated but not yet overbought, and the stock remains well below its 200SMA of $127.70, leaving significant upside room. With NVDA down 14% and regulatory overhang from the China chip probe, semiconductor weakness likely extends over multiple sessions. Volume at 1.2x average is building.

closed_trades.thesis: SLV showed relative strength vs SPY today, gaining 0.59% while SPY fell 1.01%. In extreme fear environments with 10Y yields at 5.12%, precious metals act as a safe haven. Silver benefits from both risk-off flows and industrial demand. SLV is one of the only green assets on the watchlist, showing strong relative strength of +1.60% vs SPY today.

UVIX surged 18.23% today as VIX broke above 22.91 with the market in Extreme Fear. NVDA earnings this week represent a binary event that could spike volatility further, especially with chip smuggling headlines adding uncertainty. With 10Y yields at 5.15% compressing multiples and multiple mega-cap earnings on deck (DIS, HD, NVDA all reporting), volatility has room to expand toward 28-30 VIX levels, pushing UVIX toward $52.

GOOGL is showing clear relative strength vs SPY today (+0.8% vs -0.31%), outperforming by 1.11%. As NVDA faces structural headwinds from leadership chaos and China export bans, GOOGL stands to benefit as the most vertically-integrated AI player with custom TPU chips and no China exposure risk. Consumer Discretionary and Tech leading sector rotation supports mega-cap tech positioning. Extreme Fear at 10 often produces 3-5% bounces in quality names within a week.

Leveraged inverse Nasdaq ETF rallied 2.29% today and momentum favors continuation as tech faces multiple headwinds: Nvidia governance crisis, MSFT system outages, chip export policy tightening. VIX at 25.46 with UVIX up 15.21% today confirms volatility expansion. XLK lagging at -0.91% today and F&G at 11 extreme fear suggest more downside before stabilization. Short-duration hold to manage decay risk.
